items.prompt_md: For a string of length `n`, how many possible palindrome centers must expand-around-center try?
options: `n`, one per character
`2n - 1`: `n` characters (odd length) plus `n - 1` gaps between neighbours (even length)
`n / 2`, because a palindrome is symmetric
`n^2`, one per substring
items.answer: `2n - 1`: `n` characters (odd length) plus `n - 1` gaps between neighbours (even length)
items.explanation_md: Even-length palindromes sit in the gaps between two characters, so you need a center for each gap too. Only trying `n` centers is the classic bug; `n^2` is the number of substrings, which this technique avoids enumerating.

items.prompt_md: Which input breaks a solution that only tries odd centers (`l = r = c`)?
options: A string such as `zz` or `noon`, whose longest palindrome has even length
A string with all distinct letters
A string of length 1
A string with an odd number of characters
items.answer: A string such as `zz` or `noon`, whose longest palindrome has even length
items.explanation_md: An even palindrome has no single middle character. Distinct letters still work (answer length 1) and odd-length strings are exactly what odd centers find.

items.prompt_md: What is the worst-case time of expand-around-center on a string of length `n`?
options: O(n), because each character is visited once
O(n log n), because expansions halve the range
O(n^3), because of the nested loops plus comparison
O(n^2), reached for example by a string of one repeated letter
items.answer: O(n^2), reached for example by a string of one repeated letter
items.explanation_md: There are about `2n` centers, and an expansion can walk up to `n / 2` steps, so quadratic is the worst case. Cubic comes from the brute force that re-verifies each substring from scratch.

items.prompt_md: What extra space does expand-around-center need, not counting the returned string?
options: O(n^2) for a table of palindromic substrings
O(n) for a reversed copy of the string
O(1): just a few integers for the pointers and the best span
O(log n) for the recursion stack
items.answer: O(1): just a few integers for the pointers and the best span
items.explanation_md: No table and no reversed copy are required; the pointers carry all the state. The O(n^2) table belongs to the DP alternative.

items.prompt_md: What is the time complexity of the brute force that checks every substring by comparing it with its reverse?
options: O(n^2), because there are n^2 substrings
O(n^3): O(n^2) substrings times O(n) to compare each
O(n log n), because comparison is logarithmic
O(2^n), because each character is in or out
items.answer: O(n^3): O(n^2) substrings times O(n) to compare each
items.explanation_md: The enumeration is quadratic, and each check costs linear time, so the total is cubic. Treating the check as O(1) is the common slip.

items.prompt_md: After the `while` loop finishes expanding (the pointers have already stepped past the last matching pair), what is the palindrome's length?
options: `r - l - 1`, since both pointers overshot by one
`r - l`
items.answer: `r - l - 1`, since both pointers overshot by one
items.explanation_md: At exit, `s[l]` and `s[r]` are the first mismatching pair (or out of bounds), so the palindrome is `l + 1 .. r - 1`, which has `r - l - 1` characters. `r - l + 1` is only right if you step back first.

items.prompt_md: Using the same overshoot convention, where does the best palindrome start in the original string?
options: At index `l`
At index `l - 1`
At index `r - l`
At index `l + 1`
items.answer: At index `l + 1`
items.explanation_md: The pointer `l` is one past the left end, so the palindrome starts at `l + 1` and the slice is `s[l + 1 : l + 1 + length]`.

items.prompt_md: On `racecar`, expanding from the odd center at index 3 ends with which values of `l` and `r`?
options: `l = 0`, `r = 6`, giving length 6
`l = 3`, `r = 3`, giving length 1
`l = 2`, `r = 4`, giving length 3
items.explanation_md: Every mirrored pair matches all the way out: `e`, `c-c`, `a-a`, `r-r`. The loop stops only when `l` falls off at `-1` and `r` at `7`, so the whole word of length 7 is returned.

items.prompt_md: Why does the DP table `is_pal[i][j]` use more memory than expand-around-center even though both are O(n^2) time?
options: The DP also needs a recursion stack of depth n^2
The table stores an entry for every pair `(i, j)`, O(n^2) cells, while the center method keeps only a few pointers
The table is needed to reverse the string
Expand-around-center is actually O(n^3) in memory
items.answer: The table stores an entry for every pair `(i, j)`, O(n^2) cells, while the center method keeps only a few pointers
items.explanation_md: Both visit about n^2 pairs of positions, but the DP remembers all of them whereas expansion forgets each center the moment it finishes.

items.prompt_md: How does expand-around-center relate to the opposite-ends palindrome check of the earlier two-pointers lesson?
options: The same equal-characters test, but the pointers move apart from a center instead of moving together from the ends
It is the identical algorithm, just renamed
It never compares characters, only counts them
It requires the string to be sorted first
items.answer: The same equal-characters test, but the pointers move apart from a center instead of moving together from the ends
items.explanation_md: Opposite ends answers a yes/no question for one whole string in O(n). Expanding from centers asks 'how far does the mirror extend here?' for every center.

items.prompt_md: Manacher's algorithm finds the longest palindromic substring in O(n). In an interview, what is the reasonable stance?
options: Always implement it, since O(n^2) is never acceptable
Ignore it, since it is incorrect for even-length palindromes
Use it only when the string contains digits
Know it exists and what it improves on, but expand-around-center is the expected answer
items.answer: Know it exists and what it improves on, but expand-around-center is the expected answer
items.explanation_md: Manacher reuses mirror information from earlier centers to avoid redundant expansion; it is intricate and rarely required. Mentioning it shows depth; coding the quadratic version correctly shows the core skill.

items.prompt_md: In the string `aaaa`, how many palindromic substrings (counting each position range separately) are there?
options: 4, one per character
6, the number of pairs
10: four of length 1, three of length 2, two of length 3, one of length 4
16, since every substring is palindromic and there are n^2
items.answer: 10: four of length 1, three of length 2, two of length 3, one of length 4
items.explanation_md: Every substring of identical letters is a palindrome, and the number of substrings is `n(n + 1) / 2 = 10`. Counting only single letters or pairs misses the longer ones; `n^2` over-counts.

items.prompt_md: Given a text of at most 3000 characters, return the longest contiguous stretch that reads the same forwards and backwards. Extra memory should stay constant.
options: Build an `n x n` boolean table of substrings
Expand two pointers outward from each of the 2n - 1 centers
Sort the characters and group duplicates
A fixed-size window of the answer length
items.answer: Expand two pointers outward from each of the 2n - 1 centers
items.explanation_md: A mirror stretch is determined by its middle, so grow from each middle. The table works but costs O(n^2) memory; sorting loses the order; the answer length is unknown, so no fixed window.

items.prompt_md: Count how many contiguous pieces of a short word read the same in both directions, counting repeats at different positions separately.
options: Expand two pointers outward from each of the 2n - 1 centers and count every successful expansion step
Count the frequency of each letter
Binary search on the number of pieces
Reverse the word and compare once
items.answer: Expand two pointers outward from each of the 2n - 1 centers and count every successful expansion step
items.explanation_md: Every successful expansion step from a center is exactly one more palindromic substring, so counting them gives the total in O(n^2). Letter frequencies and a single reversal cannot count substrings.

items.prompt_md: Decide whether an entire phrase, after stripping punctuation, is a palindrome, using O(1) extra space.
options: Expand two pointers outward from each of the 2n - 1 centers
A DP over all substrings
Sort and compare
Two pointers starting at the two ends and moving toward each other
items.answer: Two pointers starting at the two ends and moving toward each other
items.explanation_md: One yes/no question about the whole string is a straight opposite-ends walk in O(n). Expanding from every center does far more work than needed.

items.prompt_md: Find the length of the longest palindromic **subsequence** of a string (characters need not be adjacent).
options: Expand two pointers outward from each of the 2n - 1 centers
Two pointers from both ends only
2D DP over index ranges
A fixed-size window
items.answer: 2D DP over index ranges
items.explanation_md: Characters can be skipped, so a mirror is no longer centered on a contiguous run and expansion breaks. The standard solution is a range DP, `dp[i][j]`.

items.prompt_md: Split a string into the fewest pieces such that every piece is a palindrome.
options: Expand two pointers outward from each of the 2n - 1 centers alone, taking the longest at each step
1D DP over prefixes, using palindrome checks as a helper
A fixed-size window
A hash map of letter counts
items.answer: 1D DP over prefixes, using palindrome checks as a helper
items.explanation_md: Greedily taking the longest palindrome can be suboptimal, so you need DP over split points. Center expansion is only a fast way to know which pieces are palindromes.

items.prompt_md: List every substring of a short log line that is a palindrome of length at least 3.
options: Expand two pointers outward from each of the 2n - 1 centers and record each span of length 3 or more
Prefix sums of character codes
A monotonic stack of letters
Two sorted pointers moving only right
items.answer: Expand two pointers outward from each of the 2n - 1 centers and record each span of length 3 or more
items.explanation_md: Each expansion from a center produces nested palindromes, so reporting spans of length 3+ is a natural by-product. Prefix sums and stacks do not capture mirroring.

items.prompt_md: Return the longest substring that has no repeated letters.
options: Expand two pointers outward from each of the 2n - 1 centers
A DP table over all substrings
Sort the letters first
A variable-size sliding window with a set or map of letters inside
items.answer: A variable-size sliding window with a set or map of letters inside
items.explanation_md: The condition is about duplicates inside a contiguous range, which a window maintains; mirroring is irrelevant. Expanding from centers solves a different problem.

items.prompt_md: Check whether two words are anagrams of each other.
options: Expand two pointers outward from each of the 2n - 1 centers
Two pointers from both ends
Compare letter-frequency counts with a hash map or 26-slot array
A DP over substrings
items.answer: Compare letter-frequency counts with a hash map or 26-slot array
items.explanation_md: Anagram equality is about multiset content, not order, so counting letters is the right tool; palindromes are about order.

items.prompt_md: Test whether a string can become a palindrome by deleting at most one character.
options: Expand two pointers outward from each of the 2n - 1 centers for every center
Two pointers from the ends, with one allowed skip on a mismatch
A full 2D DP table
A min-heap of characters
items.answer: Two pointers from the ends, with one allowed skip on a mismatch
items.explanation_md: A single whole-string check with one retry is linear; trying every center is overkill and the DP uses quadratic space for no gain.

items.prompt_md: A memory-limited device must report the longest symmetric run in a 5000-character line (symmetric around some middle). Quadratic time is fine; extra memory must be O(1).
options: Expand two pointers outward from each of the 2n - 1 centers
The O(n^2)-space palindrome DP table
Brute-force check of every substring against its reverse (O(n^3))
Build a trie of all suffixes
items.answer: Expand two pointers outward from each of the 2n - 1 centers
items.explanation_md: Quadratic time with constant memory is exactly the center-expansion profile. The DP table needs quadratic memory, brute force is cubic, and a suffix trie is far heavier.

items.prompt_md: Merge several sorted lists of numbers into one sorted list, always taking the smallest front element.
options: Expand two pointers outward from each of the 2n - 1 centers
Two pointers from both ends
A sliding window
A min-heap holding one front element from each list
items.answer: A min-heap holding one front element from each list
items.explanation_md: 'Always take the smallest of several candidates' is a heap job. Nothing mirrors around a center.
